note: Explain This Screen. Keyed by the media src in experience.json. Regions are normalized 0-1 against the image's own pixels: x/y is the top-left corner, w/h the size. `label` names the region in two or three words; `note` says what a reader should take from it. Nothing here restates a number that is already legible in the screenshot as if it were a claim — the numbers belong to whatever tenant was captured.

regions.label: ThreatScore
regions.note: One posture number for the whole estate, so a leader has something to track between reviews rather than a list that only an engineer can read.

regions.label: The command strip
regions.note: Findings, failed checks, assets monitored, open POA&Ms and scan freshness on one line. Scan freshness is the one that matters most: it tells you whether everything else on this screen is current.

regions.label: Four lenses on one graph
regions.note: Exposure, identity, threats and compliance are views of the same underlying data, not four separate products. Switching lens re-weights what the map emphasises.

regions.label: Threat map
regions.note: Regions sized by severity-weighted risk rather than by finding count, so one critical exposure outweighs a hundred low ones. The arcs are correlated pathways between regions.

regions.label: Regional intelligence
regions.note: Drilling into one provider and region: its own risk score, seven-day trend, and the assets behind it. This is the bridge from a picture to something you can assign.

regions.label: Finding severity mix
regions.note: The shape of the risk, not just its size. A region scoring 85 on seven medium findings is a different conversation from one scoring 85 on a single critical.

regions.label: Top regions
regions.note: Ranked by contribution to the score, so remediation starts where it moves the number.
